title: March: Lightening Up
coreMove: When one escape route closes, trace the next comfort by its aftertaste: if it dulls pain while shrinking health, quiet, or connection, it is substitute consumption.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers using food as the first available comfort
exampleSpecs.stakes: Pizza, chocolate, and ice cream can soften grief while making the body feel worse.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show food as a substitute comfort and body feedback as the honest signal.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who use passive media to fill silence
exampleSpecs.stakes: The March television ban creates space for reading, podcasts, and honest quiet.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show television as a silence-filler and the ban as a way back to presence.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers with a permission list that can still hide impulse
exampleSpecs.stakes: Approved purchases can still become stockpiling unless quality and current need guide them.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show an allowed purchase slowed down by the need-now test.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers surprised by old coping urges
exampleSpecs.stakes: Alcohol cravings can return under stress without erasing prior progress.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show the craving as an old coping pathway reactivated by pain.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers who perform normal for most people
exampleSpecs.stakes: Selective honest support gives grief a real channel without requiring public disclosure.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show narrow trusted support as healthier than broad performance.

exampleSpecs.audience: readers replacing passive watching with active attention
exampleSpecs.stakes: A month without television can redirect time toward podcasts, reading, friends, and quiet.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show the aftertaste of a screen-free evening rather than a moral victory.
